query: How can Conley bounds or partial-identification methods be implemented to quantify bias from unobserved confounders in staggered DiD of capital regulation?

response.query: How can Conley bounds or partial-identification methods be implemented to quantify bias from unobserved confounders in staggered DiD of capital regulation?
response.answer: Conley bounds and partial-identification methods can quantify bias from unobserved confounders in staggered DiD by providing bounds for causal estimates, even with limited data. These methods help assess the sensitivity of results to unmeasured variables.

results.title: Methodological Challenges for Research on Racial Bias in Police ...
results.content: # Methodological Challenges for Research on Racial Bias in Police Shootings. In this essay, we review the evidence to date (as of early 2024) on racial bias in police shootings, focusing on the data and methodological challenges that exist for research on this topic. Research on racial bias in police shootings tends to use some form of benchmark or outcome test, both of which face important inferential challenges. For instance, if police have a lower threshold to shoot in the areas with the most gun violence, and White civilians are rarely encountered in such spots, then racial differences in outcome rates might reflect place-based differences in perceptions of danger rather than racial bias. Research on racial bias in police shootings faces challenges in both data quality and modeling. We have surveyed four broad ways through which research on racial bias in police shootings can be improved: better data, better methods, clearer definitions and estimands, and the use of bounding and sensitivity analyses.
